articles.full_text:
VISAKHAPATNAM: Severe cyclonic storm Akvan may have limited impact on
Andhra Pradesh, affecting two to three north coastal districts of the state.
The Severe Cyclonic Storm “Akvan” over the westcentral Bay of Bengal has altered its trajectory and moving towards north-northwestward and cross north Andhra Pradesh and south
Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri, near Gopalpur in Odisha, by noon on Friday, November 20, prompting Odisha to go on high alert.
The India Meteorological Department has revised its forecast for the cyclone's trajectory and intensity
Cyclonic storm Akvan, the third cyclone of 2026, is moving towards Odisha coast, bringing some relief to Andhra Pradesh farmers after initial forecasts said the severe cyclone could hit Andhra coast and cause extensive damage.
Andhra Pradesh had been hit by cyclonic storms Arnab and Murasu within a week, with the back-to-back cyclones causing extensive damage to crops and infrastructure in the state's coastal districts.
Initially the weather agency forecast that the cyclone would cross land between, Nellore and Tuni, and again forecast that Nellore and Visakhapatnam, as a very severe cyclonic. It altered the forecast and said the landfall would be between Narsapur and Puri close to Gopalpur.
India Meteorological Department (IMD) has revised its initial forecast, saying isolated extremely heavy rainfall under a red alert is likely only in Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Parvathipuram Manyam districts on Thursday.
Earlier seven districts, Kakinada, Srikakulam, Vizianagaram,Parvathipuram Manayam, Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju (ASR), and Ankapalle are covered by the red-alert category (extremely heavy rainfall) for Thursday and Friday (November 19 and 20).
Heavy rainfall and winds are expected, prompting alerts for Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, and Parvathipuram Manyam districts
Now, the IMD forecast that Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, and Parvathipuram Manyam districts are covered by the red alert category on Thursday (November 19).
There is no red alert for Andhra Pradesh on Friday (November 20), when the system is likely to cross the coast near Gopalpur in Odisha. But there is an orange alert (heavy to very heavy rainfall) for Srikakulam and Parvathipuram Manyam districts on November 20.
Isolated places in Visakhapatnam, Vizianagaram and ASR districts may receive heavy rainfall on Friday.
Meanwhile, the system over the westcentral Bay of Bengal moved northwards with the speed of 13 kmph during past six hours and lay centered over the same region, about 390km east-southeast of Narsapur (Andhra Pradesh), 320km south-southeast of Kalingapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 410km south of Gopalpur (Odisha) and 470km south of Puri (Odisha) and 610km east-northeast of Chennai (Tamil Nadu).
It is likely to move north-northwestward and cross north Andhra Pradesh and Yanam and south Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri, close to Gopalpur, by noon of Friday (November 20) with the maximum sustained wind speed of 90-100kmph gusting to 110kmph.
Few parts of the north coastal Andhra Pradesh experienced showers on Thursday. The gales with speeds reaching 60 to 80 prevailed at isolated places in coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam on Thursday. The intensity of the wind may increase on Friday.
Srikakulam and Vizianagaram district administrations are on high alert ahead of Cyclone Akvan, which is expected to cross the coast near Gopalpur in Odisha on Friday. The officials have visited a few villages near the Andhra Pradesh-Odisha border, to review preparedness.
Srikakulam was severely affected by recent cyclones Arnab and Murasu as Ichchapuram, Sompeta and other areas faced flooding in Bahuda after the cyclones and heavy rains in Odisha. The district administration decided to deploy NDRF and SDRF teams to the vulnerable areas for relief and rescue operations.
